reasoning: Set A has the stronger quant design. It hand-writes almost every method and checks each against a reference implementation, which fits the learn-by-building persona. It calibrates the test protocol on synthetic data with planted answers, uses strong baselines (EWMA/GARCH/HAR, linear before ML), runs purged walk-forward validation, pre-registers everything, keeps separate forward holdouts, and scopes PPO as a meta-allocator over five classical sleeves. It also hands every beats-chance claim to null-hypothesis-testing by name, with H0/H1, the null, alpha and the correction family written out at each requirement. That rigor comes at a heavy price. About 2,200 lines of spec and architecture, plus six idea files, are far more than a solo learner can work from. The brief is still Stage-1-centric ('later stages undecided', success criteria for Stage 1 only, Goals 5/6 stretched to cover Stages 4-6). Several component rows and idea files are stale or contradict later decisions (PPO-03 vs AD-34, MPS/rented-GPU wording, the HRP reference). Broken code fences in architecture.md make the whole Decisions, Risks and Changelog section render as a code block. Set B is about a quarter of the length and consistent across brief, spec and architecture. It plans all six stages around one shared evaluation protocol (as-of view, locked holdout, costs, caps) and an append-only test ledger. TEST-01 makes every claim go through null-hypothesis-testing, and each comparison step names the skill again. B is weaker on quant detail: a 504-day window for about 500 stocks (N/T near 1), only trailing/EWMA volatility baselines, an undefined forward-residual target, a stock-level PPO with about 200 decisions, no synthetic calibration, and less hand-writing (LightGBM, CVXPY, a PyTorch GRU). Still, it is far easier to read, navigate and start building from, and it has fewer consistency defects. B wins on overall score.

strengths: Exceptional statistical rigor: synthetic calibration of the whole Stage 4 protocol (CAL-01/02), planted-signal checks for networks (SYN-10) and PPO (SYN-12), pre-registered feature register, purged and embargoed walk-forward, separate forward holdouts per stage

Strong fit to the learn-by-building persona: nearly every method is hand-written in NumPy with eigh as the only library routine, then checked against scikit-learn, CVXPY, PyPortfolioOpt, arch, PyTorch or Stable-Baselines3 (REF-01 to REF-14), enforced by AST and import tests

Every beats-chance claim names the null-hypothesis-testing skill at its step, with H0/H1, null construction, alpha, Holm family and data split (EDA-06, OOS-10/11, LIN-03, MLT-04, VEVAL-04, RET-04, FDP-04, RSK-04, PPO-07, forward tests)
Correct worked numeric examples and KKT-based acceptance criteria (ALLOC-01, ALLOC-04, HRP-04, PRICE-04, VOL-01/02, SYN-02)
Realistic Stage 6 scope (PPO meta-allocator over 5 classical sleeves) and candid risks (low forward power, expect 'no improvement', subscription needed to 2029)
Concrete data-source comparison table with a budget-compliant choice (Sharadar $39/month with permaticker)
weaknesses: Grossly oversized for a solo learner: spec 1,029 lines, architecture 1,194 lines, plus six idea files that repeat and partly contradict the spec
Brief left Stage-1-centric: 'later stages undecided', success criteria only for data, no goals for forecasting or agents
Broken code fences in architecture.md render Cross-cutting concerns, Decisions, Risks and Changelog as code blocks
Stale coverage rows and headings left over from earlier stages (claims, reporting, 'Within Stages 2-4')
Spec and architecture disagree on the role of framework PPO runs (PPO-03/summary vs AD-34)
Spec summary is a single dense wall of text; no explicit build order
Forward holdouts push final Stage 4-6 answers to 2029, a long wait with heavy machinery for a learning project

strengths: Compact and coherent: brief, spec and architecture agree, with goals mapped to stages and success criteria for every stage
One shared evaluation protocol (EVAL: calendar, next-day execution, costs at 0/10/25 bps, caps, locked 3-year holdout) and an append-only SQLite ledger used by every stage

Look-ahead and holdout enforced in code through AsOfView and HoldoutToken, plus a poisoned-future fuzz test
Honest handling of unknown delisting returns: −30% and 0% sensitivity brackets instead of a single guessed value

weaknesses: 504-day window for about 500 stocks gives N/T near 1, so the sample covariance is near-singular

Less hand-writing than the persona prefers: LightGBM feature model, CVXPY min-variance, PyTorch GRU with no hand-written check
Stock-level PPO over a 520-slot universe with about 200 monthly decisions, and no synthetic known-answer environment
